full_judgment:
Krishna Debnath J.: This Criminal Appeal No. 55 of 2008 by leave is direct-ed against the judgment and order dated 13.08.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3589 of 2005 (heard analogous with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7578 of 2005) making the Rule absolute and quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 & C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 of the court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under section 138 of the Negotiate Instruments Act, 1881. 

 2. The relevant facts of the case for disposal of the Criminal Appeal are that the appellant lodged a complaint on 04.01.2005 being C.R. Case No. of 2005 before the chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, against the respondent stating, inter-alia, that the Medidrive Limited is a general trading company dealing in medical equipments since long. The petitioner supplied one unit 500 MA X-Ray machine (Model: Aliengers 525 DX/FC/All pose/611 TV) and one unit 3 channel ECG system (Model: P80 Interpretive, Origin: Esaote S.P.A. of stay) to the accused worth Tk. 31,30,000/- under an agreement dated 10.11.2003. As per terms of the agreement he accused made down payment of 30% of the total price amounting to Tk. 9,39,000/- and the accused promised to pay the remaining amount of Tk. 21,91,000/- as per terms of the agreement in 6(six) equal installments for which the accused issued five post dated cheques in favour of the complainant-petitioner drawn on Oriental Bank Limited and the cheque for the sixth installment of payment was not issued by the accused, according to him, for shortage of leaves in the cheque book, which he promised to issue soon after obtaining a new cheque book, but he never issued the said cheque ultimately. The petitioner by a letter dated 16.10.2005 requested the accused to issue the cheque for the sixth installment but he did not issue the same. On 09.11.2004 Medidrive Limited presented the second cheque No. 2791387 dated 09.11.2004 for Tk. 3,65,166.77 to the Oriental Bank Ltd, Gulshan Branch, Dhaka through their bank Jamuna Bank Limited, Mohakhali Branch, Dhaka, for encashment, but the Oriental Bank Limited returned the cheque without payment on three occasions namely, 09.11.2004, 20.11.2004 and 22.11.2004 due to insufficiency of fund in the account of the drawer of the cheque and the matter was informed to the accused accordingly. The complainant repeatedly requested the accused to arrange payment of the amount covered by the said cheque and the accued made verbal commitments several times to pay the outstanding amount but he did not keep the words. The complainant finally on 06.12.2004 sent a legal notice by registered post with N/D to the accused requesting him to arrange payment of Tk.3,65,166.77 covered by the above mentioned cheque within 15 days of receipt of the said legal notice, but the accused did not pay the amounts in spite of receiving the notice. accused as part payment of the above mentioned dishonored cheque provided a new cheque No. 0001544179 dated 08.12.2004 for Tk. 1,00,000/- only drawn on Standard Chartered Bank, Dhaka, the said cheque was also returned unpaid for insufficiency of fund when presented for encashment, and hence the case. 

 4. The appellant initiated another proceeding on 24.01.2005 being C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 under section 420/406 of the Penal Code against the accused respondent. 

 5. The respondent moved before the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3589 of 2005 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal procedure for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 and obtained Rule and stay. 

 6. The Rule was heard along with the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7578 of 2005 obtained by the same accused respondent in an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 under Section 420 of the Penal Code, and both the Rules were made absolute by the same judgment and order of the High Court Division which was impugned in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 301 of 2007. 

 8. He further submits that upon a misconception of law the High Court Division found want of cause of action as the com-plaint was filed beyond 15 days though Section 141(b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act clearly stipulated that the complaint has to be filed within 30 days of the accrual of cause of action. 

 9. He lastly submits that the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that C.R. Case No 128 of 2005 and C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 are on different cause of action and at any rate C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 being the earlier cannot be affected by filing of C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005." 

 10. In support of the appeal, Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellants submits that it appears that the appellant presented the cheque on 09.11.2004, 20.11.2004 and 22.11.2004 but after the cheque was dishonored for the last time, on 06.12.2004 the appellant sent a legal notice by registered post with AID to the respondent, within the statutory period and filed the case within time. 

 11. He further submits that the appellant served a legal notice within 15(fifteen) days of the receipt of the information of return of the cheque in question. So, the question when it was received is not at all material for filing the case and nondisclosure of such a date cannot be a ground for quashing the proceeding. Upon a misconception of law the High Court Division found want of cause of action, he added. 

 12. He lastly submits that the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 and C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 are on different causes of action and at any rate C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 being the earlier case can not be affected by filing of C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005. 

 13. In support of his contention he has referred to the case of Nizamalin Mahmood VS Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan and another 60 DLR (AD) 195 wherein it was observed "Since the Ate of receipt is a question of fact to 6e ascertained at the time of trial non-disclosure of such fact in the complaint petition cannot render the proceeding liable to 6e quashed to great prejudice of the complainant who is entitled to prove leis case on evidence." 

 14. He also referred the cases Habibur Rahman VS. State 53 DLR (AD), 111, Faridul Alam VS. the state and another 12 MLR (AD) 132, Munshi Md. Rashed Kamal VS. Abdus Salam 10 BLC (AD) 186, Securities and Exchange Commission VS. Abu Teyeb 55 DLR (AD) 47, in support of his contention. 

 15. Mr. Omar Sadat, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent attempted to support the impugned judgment and order but finds it difficult to support the findings of the High Court Division. Though he has referred the cases of Supreme Court of India. 

 (b) The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice, in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, and 

 (c) The drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of the said notice. 

 19. On perusal of the aforesaid provision of law it appears that the appellant complainant filed his complaint within the purview of section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881. It is not possible to know about the date of receipt of the notice for the complainant and such a question of fact cannot be decided in a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in view of the decision of this Court in the cases of Nizamuddin Mahmood Vs Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan and another 60 DLR (AD) 195, Abdul Quader Chowdhury VS state 28 DLR (AD) 38. 

 20. We also find that the C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 and C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 are on different causes of action and at any rate C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 being the earlier case cannot be affected by filing of C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005. 

 23. The appeal is therefore, allowed. The impugned judgment and order dated 13.08.2006 of the High Court Division is set aside and proceeding of the C.R. Case No. 14 of 2005 and C.R. Case No. 128 of 2005 shah continue.
